evidence.excerpt: Running a full FEM simulation for each combination of insulator geometry and pollution condition is computationally expensive for grid-scale insulator fleet assessments. This paper investigates whether a gradient-boosted regression model trained on an FEM-generated dataset can accurately predict peak tangential electric field values. The training dataset comprised 2 400 2D FEM simulations varying six parameters: shed diameter ratio, pitch, shed count, pollution conductivity, film thickness, and power frequency voltage. An 80/20 train–test split was used; hyperparameters were tuned by fivefold cross-validation. The trained model predicted peak field values with a mean absolute error of 0.031 kV/mm and R² = 0.97 on the held-out test set, with inference times under 2 ms. The approach was validated against an independent set of 60 FEM cases not used in training, confirming generalisability within the parameter ranges studied. Limitations at extrapolation boundaries are discussed.
